recipes.name: Versagel & Castor Facial Gel
recipes.description: Simple lip gloss base using Versagel. High shine, non-sticky finish. Add flavor oil or fragrance and mica for color.
recipes.notes: Versagel is thick — warm gently between palms or in a warm water bath to make it workable. Castor oil adds extra gloss and slip. Mica can be stirred in for tinted gloss.

recipes.name: Shea & Sunflower Body Butter
recipes.description: The simplest whipped body butter — just shea, a liquid oil, vitamin E, and fragrance. Fluffy, melt-on-skin texture.
recipes.notes: No heat needed if shea is already soft/fluffy. Sub sunflower with any light liquid oil (apricot kernel, sweet almond, hemp seed).

recipes.name: Shea & Sunflower Body Butter
recipes.description: Adds arrowroot or corn starch to reduce the greasy feel — silkier finish on skin.
recipes.notes: Corn starch works as a 1:1 sub for arrowroot. Whip shea first, add oil gradually, fold in starch last.

recipes.name: Shea & Mango Body Butter
recipes.description: More complex whipped butter with multiple oils for a richer skin feel.
recipes.notes: Coconut oil may require brief melt in warm weather. Mango butter adds firmness and a smoother melt point.

recipes.name: Aloe Vera Body Gel
recipes.description: A water-based gel formulation utilizing xanthan gum for viscosity. Suitable for oil-prone or sensitive skin types. Requires broad-spectrum preservation.
recipes.notes: Xanthan gum is a thickener not in current inventory — recipe still works without it but will be thinner. Preservative required since water-based.
recipes.process:
1. Mix the distilled water and vegetable glycerin in a container.
2. Sprinkle the xanthan gum over the liquid and whisk or blend to incorporate.
3. Allow the mixture to sit for at least 20 minutes to let the thickener fully hydrate.
4. Stir in the liquid Germall Plus once the gel is formed.
5. Package the final gel in a clean container.

recipes.name: Mct & Rosehip Body Oil
recipes.description: A lightweight, anhydrous body oil blend designed for rapid absorption. Formulated without a water phase to eliminate the need for preservation.
recipes.notes: Sub MCT with fractionated coconut or apricot kernel. Rosehip is not in inventory but optional — sub with hemp seed.
recipes.process:
1. Combine all ingredients in a small beaker or directly into the final storage bottle.
2. Mix thoroughly by stirring if using a beaker, or by capping and shaking the bottle.
3. Apply to the skin by misting after a shower or bath.
4. Clean any surfaces accidentally misted with oil to prevent them from becoming slippery.

recipes.name: Apricot Kernel & Hemp Body Oil
recipes.description: Custom blend using on-hand oils. Hemp seed adds anti-inflammatory properties, apricot kernel absorbs quickly.
recipes.notes: All ingredients in inventory. Castor adds slip and gloss. Adjust ratios to preference.

recipes.name: Shea & Aloe Vera Body Butter
recipes.description: An emulsified body butter containing both oil and water phases for a non-greasy finish. Requires an emulsifying wax and broad-spectrum preservation.
recipes.notes: BTMS-50 (conditioning emulsifier) not in inventory. Sub with Polysorbate-20 at slightly higher % but texture will differ.
recipes.process:
1. Create a water bath by simmering roughly 3cm of water in a broad, flat pan.
2. Measure the water phase ingredients into one heat-safe beaker and the oil phase ingredients into a second heat-safe beaker.
3. Record the combined weight of the water phase beaker and its contents for later reference.
4. Place both beakers into the simmering water bath until all oil phase ingredients have completely melted.
5. Use an immersion blender to mix the ingredients, using brief bursts initially to avoid splashing.
6. Blend the mixture for approximately one minute, then transition to manual stirring.
7. Continue stirring steadily until the mixture begins to show signs of thickening or clumping.
8. Use the immersion blender for several more quick bursts while ensuring the head remains fully submerged.
9. Allow the thickened emulsion to sit while you measure the ingredients for the cooling phase.
10. Incorporate the cooling phase ingredients once the mixture has reached room temperature.
11. Transfer the finished product into a wide-mouthed tub or jar.

recipes.name: Fractionated Coconut & Sweet Almond Body Oil
recipes.description: A sprayable body oil containing mica for a reflective finish. Requires heat during formulation to ensure uniform distribution of the mica.
recipes.notes: Polysorbate-20 in inventory. Sub fractionated coconut with apricot kernel or hemp seed.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the ingredients for the heated phase in a container suitable for direct heat.
2. Heat the mixture until it reaches approximately 90°C (194°F) and the wax is completely melted.
3. Verify the wax has fully liquefied by stirring and checking for any translucent blobs.
4. Remove the container from the heat source and stir in the mica powder.
5. Continue stirring the mixture as it cools to room temperature to ensure the shimmer remains evenly distributed.
6. Incorporate the cooling phase ingredients and stir well.
7. Transfer the finished oil into a bottle equipped with a spray nozzle.

recipes.name: Shea & Coconut Body Butter
recipes.description: Partially melted shea blended with lighter oils for a less waxy finish.
recipes.notes: Heat to melt coconut oil fully, then cool to just-solidified before whipping.

recipes.name: Hemp & Aloe Vera Body Lotion
recipes.description: Water-based lotion using hemp seed and apricot kernel. Needs emulsifier — Polysorbate-20 can work at higher %.
recipes.notes: Polysorbate-20 is a light emulsifier — may need higher % for stable emulsion. Proper emulsifiers (BTMS-50, Emulsifying Wax) give better texture.

recipes.name: Aloe Vera & Polysorbate-20 Facial Mist
recipes.description: Simple face/body toner. Witch hazel tones and tightens, aloe soothes, glycerin hydrates.
recipes.notes: All ingredients in inventory. Polysorbate-20 solubilizes any added fragrance or essential oil. Preservative required — water-based product.

recipes.name: Mango & Shea Body Butter
recipes.description: A temperature-stable body butter formulated with high-melting-point waxes to maintain consistency in warm environments.
recipes.notes: Candelilla wax not in inventory. Beeswax could sub but changes texture significantly.
recipes.process:
1. Set up a water bath by simmering about 3cm of water in a wide, flat-bottomed pan.
2. Measure the water phase ingredients into one heat-safe container and the oil phase ingredients into another.
3. Note the total weight of the water phase container and its contents for later adjustment.
4. Heat both containers in the water bath until the oil phase is entirely liquid.
5. Combine and mix the phases as they begin to cool.
6. Once the mixture has reached room temperature, stir in the cooling phase ingredients.
7. Transfer the final body butter into a storage jar or tub.

recipes.name: Hemp & Aloe Vera Body Cream
recipes.description: A rich, emulsified hand cream formulated with hemp seed oil. Requires heat-assisted emulsification and preservation.
recipes.notes: BTMS-50 not in inventory. Without it, emulsion won't hold properly. Note for shopping list.
recipes.process:
1. Prepare a simmering water bath in a broad, flat-bottomed sauté pan.
2. Measure the water phase ingredients into a heat-resistant beaker and record the total weight.
3. Measure the oil phase ingredients into a separate heat-resistant beaker.
4. Heat both beakers in the water bath until all solid ingredients have melted.
5. Mix the two phases together and allow the emulsion to cool.
6. Once the cream is cool, incorporate the ingredients for the cooling phase.
7. Check the pH level to ensure it falls between 4.6 and 5.5 for optimal stability.
8. Transfer the finished cream into a suitable container.

recipes.name: Shea & Mango Body Butter
recipes.description: Seasonal scented whipped butter. Melt-and-whip method.
recipes.notes: Sweet almond oil not in inventory. Sub with apricot kernel (similar profile) or hemp seed.

recipes.name: Shea & Emulsifying Body Cream
recipes.description: A dense, emulsified foot cream utilizing jojoba oil and shea butter. Includes peppermint essential oil for a cooling effect.
recipes.notes: Cetyl alcohol thickens and gives a silky feel. Sodium lactate is a natural humectant that also adjusts pH. Requires a pH in the 4.8–5 range for preservative efficacy. Store in a wide-mouthed jar.
recipes.process:
1. Simmer about 3cm of water in a broad pan to create a water bath.
2. Measure the oil phase ingredients into a large heat-resistant beaker.
3. In a second beaker, measure out the water phase ingredients.
4. Heat both containers in the water bath for 20 to 30 minutes until the oils are melted and the water is steaming.
5. Remove the beakers from the heat and slowly incorporate the hot water into the oil mixture.
6. Stir the mixture with a silicone spatula to begin the emulsion.
7. Use an immersion blender in short bursts to mix the lotion, continuing for about one minute.
8. Transition to manual stirring and continue until the cream becomes thick and uniform.
9. Once the outside of the glass measuring cup is just warm to the touch (40°C or lower), stir in the ingredients for the cooling phase.
10. Verify that the final pH level is approximately 4.8 to 5.
11. Package the thick cream into wide-mouthed jars using a piping bag if necessary for easier filling.

recipes.name: Apricot Kernel & Plum Kernel Body Oil
recipes.description: A multi-purpose shimmer oil for the face, body, and hair, featuring plum and apricot kernel oils and iridescent mica.
recipes.notes: Original uses Crystal Clear Wax (0.5%) to suspend mica — can omit but mica will settle. Sub plum kernel with apricot kernel. No water = no preservative needed.
recipes.process:
1. Place the heated phase ingredients in a container that can withstand direct heat.
2. Warm the mixture until it reaches approximately 100°C (212°F) and the wax is fully melted.
3. Stir the liquid and check carefully to ensure no solid wax particles remain.
4. Remove the mixture from the heat and stir in the mica shimmer.
5. Continue stirring occasionally as the oil cools to room temperature.
6. Mix in the cooling phase ingredients and stir until uniform.
7. Package the oil in a bottle with a treatment pump or spray cap.

recipes.name: Hyaluronic Acid Facial Serum
recipes.description: A water-based serum formulated with hyaluronic acid for hydration. This cold-process formulation does not require heating.
recipes.notes: Hyaluronic acid here is used as a 1% pre-dissolved solution (30% of batch = 30g of that solution). Let xanthan gum hydrate for at least 20 minutes before use. Target pH 5–5.5. Preservative required.
recipes.process:
1. Measure the preservative and propanediol into a large beaker and stir until fully blended.
2. Add the thickener and silicone alternative, stirring until the mixture is uniform and hazy.
3. Incorporate all remaining ingredients and stir well.
4. Cover the container and let it sit for at least 20 minutes to allow the thickener to fully hydrate.
5. Verify that the pH level is appropriate for both skin compatibility and preservative effectiveness.
6. Transfer the serum into bottles equipped with treatment pumps or eyedroppers.

recipes.name: Shea & Coconut Hair Balm
recipes.description: Anhydrous balm for dry hair ends. Beeswax provides hold, shea and jojoba add deep conditioning.
recipes.notes: Original includes cocoa butter (15%), camellia seed oil (10%), walnut oil (6%) not in inventory. Sub with more shea and coconut. Use sparingly on hair ends only — a little goes a long way.

recipes.name: Mct Hair Solution
recipes.description: A simplified, rinse-out hair conditioner formulated with a limited ingredient list to provide slip and manageability.
recipes.notes: BTMS-50 is the key conditioning emulsifier (not in inventory). Sub MCT with fractionated coconut. Heat water and BTMS-50 together at 75–80°C; blend; cool to 40°C before adding preservative.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the distilled water and conditioning emulsifier in a heat-safe container.
2. Heat the mixture to between 75°C and 80°C until the emulsifier is fully melted.
3. Use an immersion blender to mix the ingredients until a uniform emulsion is formed.
4. Allow the mixture to cool to 40°C or lower.
5. Incorporate the panthenol, preservative, and fragrance oil once the emulsion has cooled.
6. Monitor the condition of the product for any changes in color or scent, and discard if stability is compromised.
7. Verify that the final pH level falls between 4.8 and 5.5.

recipes.name: Cocoa & Coconut Body Butter
recipes.description: Decadent whipped butter made from just cocoa butter and coconut oil — naturally scented chocolate-coconut.
recipes.notes: Melt both together, cool to near-solid, then whip with electric beaters. Chill slightly between whipping rounds. Cocoa butter not in inventory — it is the dominant ingredient. Optional: add a few drops of essential oil.

recipes.name: Mango & Coconut Body Butter
recipes.description: Firm anhydrous body butter with a natural chocolate-coconut aroma. Mica optional for a subtle shimmer.
recipes.notes: Melt together, stir continuously as it cools to custard-like texture, then pour into tin. A little goes a long way — firm texture prevents over-application. Cocoa butter not in inventory.

recipes.name: Apricot Kernel & Coconut Body Oil
recipes.description: Simple anhydrous massage oil — liquid at room temperature, glides smoothly on skin.
recipes.notes: Coconut oil melts at 24°C — it may need gentle warming to blend. Sub apricot kernel with sweet almond. Cinnamon bark essential oil used at only 0.05% (safety limit). Warm in hands before applying.

recipes.name: Argan & Essential Facial Serum
recipes.description: 100% oil-based facial serum — just argan oil and a few drops of essential oils. No preservative needed.
recipes.notes: Argan oil is not in inventory. Use 4–5 drops on face once or twice daily. Store in dark amber glass bottle. Shelf life ~1 year. For sensitive skin, start without essential oils.

recipes.name: Argan & Essential Facial Serum
recipes.description: Anti-aging facial serum with argan oil and carrot seed essential oil — rich in antioxidants.
recipes.notes: Essential oils: carrot seed + chamomile. Argan not in inventory — sub with rosehip (excellent for mature skin). Use dark glass dropper bottle. Start with 3 drops carrot seed EO; it has a strong earthy smell.

recipes.name: Rosehip & Jojoba Facial Serum
recipes.description: Two-oil healing serum for scars and hyperpigmentation. Rosehip regenerates, tamanu heals.
recipes.notes: Original uses tamanu oil (not in inventory) — sub with jojoba for a gentle, non-comedogenic version. Add 2 drops frankincense + 1 drop helichrysum EO per 15mL for enhanced healing. No heat, no preservative needed.

recipes.name: Shea & Beeswax Facial Butter
recipes.description: Rich, healing lip balm with shea butter and beeswax. Melts perfectly at body temperature.
recipes.notes: Olive oil and avocado oil not in inventory — sub with apricot kernel or sweet almond. Melt together in a double boiler, add EO off heat, pour immediately into tubes. Yields 4–5 tubes.

recipes.name: Sweet Almond & Coconut Facial Balm
recipes.description: Classic lip balm with a peppermint tingle. Cocoa butter provides natural chocolate fragrance.
recipes.notes: Sweet almond and cocoa butter not in inventory — sub almond with apricot kernel. Essential oil is peppermint (20 drops per ~49g batch). Yields ~10–11 tubes. Melt together, add EO off heat.

recipes.name: Coconut & Beeswax Body Butter
recipes.description: Simple tropical body butter — just coconut oil and beeswax. Solid at room temperature, melts on contact.
recipes.notes: Melt all together, pour into shallow tin. Original uses kukuinut and baobab oil — sub with jojoba and apricot kernel. No preservative needed (anhydrous). Coconut provides a natural tropical scent.

recipes.name: Grapeseed & Shea Body Oil
recipes.description: Fast-absorbing shimmer oil using grapeseed and a small amount of butter. Mica settles unless shaken.
recipes.notes: Grapeseed not in inventory — sub with apricot kernel or sunflower. Melt butter into oil, cool, add mica in bottle. Shake before each use. Any fine mica color works.

recipes.name: Olive & Emulsifying Body Cream
recipes.description: Gentle lotion with colloidal oatmeal and olive oil. Soothing for dry or sensitive skin.
recipes.notes: Olive oil and cocoa butter not in inventory — sub olive with sunflower or apricot kernel, cocoa butter with mango butter. Colloidal oatmeal is soothing for eczema-prone skin.

recipes.name: Polysorbate-20 & Apricot Kernel Hair Mist
recipes.description: Lightweight spray that controls frizz without weighing hair down. Polysorbate-20 disperses oil in water.
recipes.notes: Original uses camellia oil — apricot kernel is a great sub. Polysorbate-20 is in inventory. Spray sparingly; too much = greasy. Preservative required (water-based).

recipes.name: Aloe Vera & Apricot Kernel Body Mist
recipes.description: Aloe-based body spray with a touch of oil for post-shower hydration. Quick, no-rub moisture.
recipes.notes: All core ingredients in inventory. Sub grapeseed oil with apricot kernel. Shake before use if no Polysorbate-20 is added. Apply immediately after toweling off.

recipes.name: Hemp & Candelilla Body Butter
recipes.description: All-hemp seed oil body butter firmed with vegan waxes. Glassy green appearance, smooth texture.
recipes.notes: Hemp seed oil in inventory! Use double boiler — hemp has a low smoke point. Needs 3 days to cure before use. Original uses bayberry wax + candelilla wax; beeswax is a substitute (not fully vegan). Sub candelilla with more beeswax if needed.

recipes.name: Sugar & Coconut Body Scrub
recipes.description: Classic two-ingredient sugar scrub — oil and sugar. Exfoliates and moisturizes in one step.
recipes.notes: Use Polysorbate-20 (~10%) to make it rinse cleanly and reduce slip hazard. Coconut oil and apricot kernel in inventory. Keep dry — water contamination causes mold. Store outside shower.

recipes.name: Apricot Kernel & Coconut Body Oil
recipes.description: Simple warming massage oil for sore muscles. Coconut provides slip, apricot kernel absorbs well.
recipes.notes: All ingredients in inventory. Castor oil adds extra slip. Warm in hands before applying. Use ginger or peppermint EO for warming/cooling effect.

recipes.name: Shea & Emulsifying Body Cream
recipes.description: Emulsified scrub that rinses clean and leaves skin soft. Lotion base with pumice or salt exfoliants.
recipes.notes: Original adds pumice (1 tbsp) and coarse salt (1 tsp) after emulsion forms. Essential oils (lavender + fir) add fragrance. Shea butter in inventory. Use corn starch instead of pumice if needed for gentler scrub.

recipes.name: Apricot Kernel & Beeswax Body Lotion
recipes.description: Old-school cold cream style lotion. Heavier and more occlusive than modern emulsifier-based lotions.
recipes.notes: This is a cold-cream style formula — greasy and occlusive. Good as a night cream. Cool both phases separately before combining. Grapeseed oil in original — subbed with apricot kernel.

recipes.name: Cetearyl Alcohol & Sodium Cocoyl Isethionate Facial Solution
recipes.description: A gentle, low-lather facial cleanser formulated with mild surfactants and skin-soothing vitamins. Suitable for all skin types.
recipes.notes: The inspirationFormulation overviewThe ingredientsDistilled waterGlycerinCetearyl AlcoholSodium Cocoyl Isethionate (SCI)Xanthan gumVitamins B3 + B5Lactic acidLiquid Germall™ PlusRelevant links & further readingGentle Low-Lather Face CleanserSubstitutionsSimilar Formulations The inspiration This formulation was inspired by Cetaphil’s Gentle Skin Cleanser; I was really intrigued by the sh
recipes.process:
1. Combine the main water phase ingredients (Phase A) in a beaker large enough to hold the full batch.
2. In a separate container, blend the xanthan gum and a portion of the glycerin until smooth.
3. Stir in the vitamins, remaining distilled water, and lactic acid to finish Phase B.
4. Record the total weight of the Phase B beaker and its contents for later adjustment.
5. Create a water bath and heat Phases A and B, along with a small container of extra distilled water (Phase C), on a hot plate or stovetop.
6. Heat on low for roughly 20 minutes until the oil phase liquefies and all components reach a similar temperature.
7. Remove Phase A from the heat and incorporate the specified amount of hot water from Phase C.
8. Stir the mixture vigorously, ensuring you scrape the sides of the beaker until it thickens into a glossy gel.
9. Weigh the Phase B beaker, add enough hot water to replace any evaporated during heating, and then blend Phase B into the gel.
10. Stir the combined mixture gently to avoid creating bubbles, then allow it to cool to room temperature.
11. Once cool, mix in the preservative and verify the pH level is skin-compatible.
12. Transfer the finished cleanser into a pump or squeeze bottle.

recipes.name: Medium Chain Triglycerides & Medium Chain Triglycerides Facial Balm
recipes.description: An anhydrous cleansing balm formulation designed for effective removal of debris and makeup. Available in three variations.
recipes.notes: Cleansing balms are a fabulous way to cleanse the skin (they’re especially great for removing long-wearing makeup!), and they’re really easy to make. In this post I’ll teach you how to make three different simple cleansing balm formulations. Each uses just three or four easy-to-get ingredients, and I explain the purpose (and substitution options) for all of them so you’ll u
recipes.process:
1. Set up a simmering water bath in a small saucepan with about 3cm of water.
2. Measure all ingredients into a heat-safe beaker and place it in the water bath until completely melted.
3. Prepare a cooling bath by filling a bowl with ice cubes and cold water.
4. Set the beaker into the ice bath and stir continuously as it cools.
5. Once white, solid bits begin to form, remove the beaker from the ice bath and continue stirring manually to smooth the texture.
6. When the balm reaches a "trace" consistency, pour it into a jar and allow it to set for at least one hour.

recipes.name: Fractionated Coconut & Castor Facial Cream
recipes.description: A soft, clay-infused cleansing balm that transforms into an oil upon application. Designed for effective rinsing and skin softening.
recipes.notes: Substitutions As always, be aware that making substitutions will change the final product. While these swaps won’t break the recipe, you will get a different final product than I did.
recipes.process:
1. Set up a simmering water bath in a small saucepan.
2. Measure the heated phase ingredients into a heat-safe beaker and place it in the water bath until liquefied.
3. Prepare a gentle cooling bath with cold water and a single ice cube in a bowl.
4. After 20–30 minutes of heating, remove the beaker from the water bath and dry the exterior.
5. Place the beaker in the cooling bath and stir constantly until the mixture is lukewarm and safe to touch.
6. Mix in the cooling phase ingredients until fully incorporated.
7. Once the balm thickens to a "trace" consistency, pour it into jars and place them in the refrigerator to solidify.
8. Allow the product to return to room temperature before its first use.

recipes.name: Fractionated Coconut & White Kaolin Clay Facial Cream
recipes.description: A thickened cleansing balm utilizing cetearyl alcohol for improved rinse-off performance. Transforms into a milky emulsion upon contact with water.
recipes.notes: A solid 20% of white kaolin clay makes this balm-to-milk cleanser extra creamy and lovely. I recommend sticking to white clay (or mostly white clay) to keep the mess factor down. If you want a wee bit of colour you could swap 3–5% of the kaolin for a soft, smooth, coloured clay like French green clay or French pink clay , but a full swap is likely to leave your sink looking pretty icky after you u
recipes.process:
1. Create a water bath by simmering roughly 3cm of water in a small pan.
2. Measure the heated phase ingredients into a heat-safe beaker and place it in the water bath.
3. Prepare a cold ice bath in a separate bowl.
4. Heat the ingredients for 20–30 minutes until fully melted, then remove from the water bath and dry the container.
5. Set the beaker into the ice bath and stir steadily until soft solid particles begin to appear on your spatula.
6. Mix in the cooling phase ingredients and stir well.
7. Once the mixture reaches a "trace" consistency, transfer it to its final container and refrigerate until set.
8. To use, massage a small amount onto dry skin, then rinse with water to transform the balm into a milk.

recipes.name: Rose & Sweet Almond Facial Cream
recipes.description: A dense, cream-based facial cleanser formulated for gentle removal of impurities. Suitable for dry or sensitive skin.
recipes.notes: Substitutions As always, be aware that making substitutions will change the final product. While these swaps won’t break the recipe, you will get a different final product than I did.
recipes.process:
1. Prepare a simmering water bath in a broad, flat-bottomed pan.
2. Measure the water phase ingredients into one heat-safe beaker and the oil phase ingredients into another.
3. Record the total weight of the water phase beaker for later reference.
4. Heat both beakers in the water bath until the oil phase has completely melted.
5. Combine the phases and allow the mixture to cool and thicken.
6. Once room temperature, incorporate the cooling phase ingredients.
7. Verify that the final pH level is approximately 6 for optimal stability.
8. Transfer the thick cream into a wide-mouthed jar or tub.

recipes.name: White Kaolin Clay & Pink Clay Facial Solution
recipes.description: An anhydrous powder cleanser that transforms into a gentle foam when combined with water. Features light exfoliation from cranberry fiber.
recipes.notes: For added creaminess and re-fatting I also included a bit of rich coconut milk powder. You could definitely use a different powdered milk if you wanted to—cow or goat milk would also be lovely!
recipes.process:
1. Wear a dust mask to avoid inhaling fine powders.
2. Measure the dry ingredients into a small mixing bowl.
3. Drizzle the liquid ingredients over the powders and stir gently until the oils are fully coated and the mixture is uniform.
4. Transfer the powdered cleanser into a shaker bottle or a tube with a screw-on lid.
5. To use, dispense about 1/4–1/2 tsp of the powder cleanser into your palm. Add a bit of water and work it up into a lather; from there, use it as you'd use any foaming facial cleanser.

recipes.name: Cocamidopropyl Betaine & Decyl Glucoside Facial Wash
recipes.description: A foaming liquid face wash featuring turmeric extract for its anti-inflammatory properties. Utilizes gentle surfactants for a non-drying cleanse.
recipes.notes: Edit (2025-04-08) After reading this article from professional cosmetic chemist Amanda Foxon-Hill, I’d recommend using a 10% NaOH solution to raise the pH instead of L-Arginine as “chemically speaking, arginine has the capacity for introducing to the formula a level of chaos and vulnerability that sodium hydroxide simply doesn’t possess.” Remove the L-Arginine, replace it with mo
recipes.process:
1. Set up a simmering water bath in a broad, flat-pan.
2. Blend the glycerin and preservative in a beaker, then add the distilled water.
3. Note the total weight of the water phase beaker and its contents.
4. Heat the water phase in the water bath until the preservative has fully dissolved.
5. In a second beaker, stir the surfactant phase ingredients together.
6. Remove the heated water phase from the bath and add enough fresh distilled water to replace any lost to evaporation.
7. Slowly pour the water phase into the surfactant mixture and stir gently to avoid excessive bubbles.
8. Allow the mixture to cool to room temperature before stirring in the turmeric extract.
9. Package the final liquid in a bottle with a foamer pump.

recipes.name: C12-15 Alkyl Benzoate & Safflower Facial Oil
recipes.description: A jelly-to-oil cleanser utilizing PEG-40 Hydrogenated Castor Oil for efficient rinse-off. Provides a smooth skin feel without greasy residue.
recipes.notes: Substitutions As always, be aware that making substitutions will change the final product. While these swaps won’t break the recipe, you will get a different final product than I did.
recipes.process:
1. Combine all ingredients in a small, heat-safe beaker or saucepan.
2. Gently heat the mixture on the lowest possible setting until the thickener has fully liquefied.
3. Alternatively, melt the mixture in a preheated oven at 100°C (210°F) until clear.
4. Allow the jelly to cool slightly before transferring it into a squeeze tube.
5. Once fully cooled, cap the tube and store at room temperature.
6. To use, massage a squirt of the cleansing jelly into dry skin, then remove with a damp cloth.

recipes.name: Fractionated Coconut & Fractionated Coconut Facial Oil
recipes.description: A two-ingredient oil cleanser that emulsifies into a milk upon contact with water. Designed for minimal irritation and easy use.
recipes.notes: I love to include around 10% castor oil in my cleansing oil formulations—it’s a hold-over from my days trying the OCM, and I find it boosts cleansing and leaves my skin feeling lovely. I haven’t included it here in the interests of super-simple-ness, but you could easily swap out 10% of the fractionated coconut oil for castor oil if you have it.
recipes.process:
1. Measure all ingredients directly into the final storage bottle or a small beaker.
2. For versions containing hydrogenated castor oil, warm the container in a simmering water bath until the solid components melt.
3. Remove from heat and stir or shake the container until the mixture is uniform.
4. Package in an airless pump or standard bottle.
5. To use, massage a dime-sized amount of the cleanser into dry skin and remove with a damp microfibre cloth.

recipes.name: Sweet Almond & Colloidal Oatmeal Facial Cream
recipes.description: A gentle, conditioning face wash formulated with colloidal oatmeal and sweet almond oil. Maintains a skin-compatible pH level.
recipes.notes: The almondy, oaty goodness continues today with this formulation for a gentle Almond Oat Creamy Conditioning Face Wash. This formulation features soothing colloidal oatmeal, vitamin-rich sweet almond oil, and conditioning BTMS-25 ❤️ It gently cleanses the skin, leaving it feeling soft and refreshed without being drying. It can also double as a cleansing conditioner for your hair if y
recipes.process:
1. Create a simmering water bath in a wide, flat-bottomed pan.
2. Measure the water phase ingredients into one heat-safe container and the oil phase ingredients into a second one.
3. Record the starting weight of the water phase container for later volume correction.
4. Heat both containers in the water bath until the oil phase is entirely melted.
5. Combine the two phases and mix thoroughly using an immersion blender.
6. Once the emulsion has cooled and the cooling phase is added, transfer the face wash into a soft squeeze tube.
7. Verify the final pH level is approximately 5 for optimal skin compatibility.

recipes.name: Fractionated Coconut & Coco-caprylate Facial Oil
recipes.description: A natural cleansing oil utilizing polyglyceryl-4 oleate for gentle emulsification. Effective for removing sunscreen and environmental debris.
recipes.notes: This exotically-scented Sweet Magnolia Natural Cleansing Oil gently cleanses the skin, leaving your face feeling soft and nourished. It uses a new-to-me natural emulsifier and has quickly become a favourite facial cleanser for removing layers of summer sunscreen (and sweat) at the end of the day. I love the velvety way it makes my skin feel, and the scent is intoxicating. You’ll only need si
recipes.process:
1. Measure all ingredients into a small beaker or directly into the final storage bottle.
2. If using a beaker, stir the mixture until it is completely uniform.
3. If using a bottle, secure the cap and shake vigorously until blended.
4. Note that the natural emulsifier may take several minutes of steady mixing to fully incorporate.
5. Apply a small amount to dry skin and massage gently to dissolve impurities.
6. Remove the oil with a warm, damp cloth for best results.

recipes.name: White Kaolin Clay & Colloidal Oatmeal Facial Solution
recipes.description: A silk-textured powder cleanser that foams upon contact with water. Formulated with kaolin clay and colloidal oatmeal for a soothing cleanse.
recipes.notes: This soft, silky powder transforms into a creamy, sudsy cleanser when you work it up with a bit of warm water between your palms. It stars soft and velvety kaolin clay and skin-soothing oats, and you can blend up a batch in just a few moments from just six ingredients. You can customize the exfoliation level and easily make it nut free if you want to. Let’s get started!
recipes.process:
1. Put on a dust mask to ensure you do not inhale the fine powders.
2. Measure the dry ingredients into a small mixing bowl and stir until blended.
3. Drizzle the liquid ingredients over the powders and mix gently until the oils are fully absorbed and the texture is uniform.
4. Transfer the finished powder into a shaker-style container.
5. To use, mix about half a teaspoon of powder with water in your palm to create a lather before massaging onto the face.

recipes.name: Sweet Almond & White Kaolin Clay Facial Balm
recipes.description: A clay-based cleansing balm that emulsifies into a milk. Formulated with sweet almond oil and oatmeal for a nourishing effect.
recipes.notes: Substitutions As always, be aware that making substitutions will change the final product. While these swaps won’t break the recipe, you will get a different final product than I did.
recipes.process:
1. Prepare a simmering water bath in a small saucepan.
2. Measure the heated phase ingredients into a heat-safe beaker and place it in the water bath.
3. Stir occasionally while heating for 20–30 minutes to ensure the powders remain evenly distributed.
4. Once the mixture is completely melted, remove from the water bath and dry the exterior of the container.
5. Quickly stir in the cooling phase ingredients until well blended.
6. Pour the mixture into its final container and immediately place it in the refrigerator to set.
7. Allow the balm to return to room temperature before its first use.

recipes.name: Plum Kernel & Cocamidopropyl Betaine Facial Wash
recipes.description: A creamy, low-pH facial cleanser formulated with plum kernel oil and Kakadu plum powder. Designed for a gentle, non-stripping cleanse.
recipes.notes: Substitutions As always, be aware that making substitutions will change the final product. While these swaps won’t break the recipe, you will get a different final product than I did.
recipes.process:

4. Heat both containers in the water bath until all solid components have liquefied.
5. Combine the two phases and allow the resulting emulsion to thicken as it cools.
6. Once the mixture is room temperature, incorporate the cooling phase ingredients.
7. Package the thick, creamy cleanser into a wide-mouthed jar.
8. Verify that the final pH level is approximately 4.65.

recipes.name: White Kaolin Clay & Sodium Cocoyl Isethionate Facial Solution
recipes.description: A powder-to-foam cleanser featuring finely ground apricot kernel for gentle physical exfoliation. Utilizes kaolin and red clays for deep cleansing.
recipes.notes: I’ve included a small amount—a scant 1%—of ground apricot kernel powder. This is a pretty scrubby exfoliant, hence the low amount, which is further tempered by grinding it down to an even smaller particle size. All the same, if you have very sensitive skin you may want to halve the exfoliant or remove it altogether, replacing it with more clay or a dried botanical of choice.
recipes.process:
1. Wear a dust mask to protect yourself from fine particles.
2. Combine all ingredients and mix thoroughly until the texture is uniform and the liquids are absorbed.
3. Transfer the powder into a bottle with a narrow neck or a sifter lid for easy dispensing.
4. To use, work about half a teaspoon of the powder with a little water in your hands to create a foam before applying to the skin.

recipes.name: Cocoa & Coconut Facial Cream
recipes.description: A dense, cream-based cleanser formulated with cocoa butter and virgin coconut oil. Designed for high emolliency and gentle cleansing.
recipes.notes: Substitutions As always, be aware that making substitutions will change the final product. While these swaps won’t break the recipe, you will get a different final product than I did.
recipes.process:
1. Create a water bath by simmering roughly 3cm of water in a broad, flat-bottomed pan.

4. Remove from heat and add enough hot distilled water to bring the mixture back to its original weight.
5. Stir the mixture steadily with a silicone spatula until it is completely uniform.
6. Once the cooling phase has been added, transfer the cleanser into a squeeze tube or bottle.
7. Apply a small amount to either damp or dry skin and rinse thoroughly.

recipes.name: Finely Powdered Sodium Cocoyl Isethionate & Finely Powdered Sodium Cocoyl Isethionate Facial Solution
recipes.description: A solid syndet cleansing bar utilizing Sodium Cocoyl Isethionate and corn starch. Formulated to maintain a skin-compatible pH of 5.5.
recipes.notes: Lastly, a preservative to keep things safe and stable. In 2020 I used Liquid Germall™ Plus, and in 2025 I used Optiphen™ Plus. This is a fairly easy-to-preserve formulation, so you could swap the preservative if you need/want to. Optiphen™ or Euxyl® PE 9010 would be good, easy options.
recipes.process:
1. Wear a dust mask and measure the dry ingredients into a mixing bowl, stirring until blended.
2. Add the wet phase ingredients to the bowl.
3. Use gloved hands to knead the mixture until it forms a stiff, mouldable dough.
4. If the texture is too sticky, add small amounts of clay or starch; if too dry, add a few drops of surfactant or water.
5. Press the dough into a mould or shape it by hand into flat-topped bars.
6. Allow the bars to air-dry and harden for 3 to 5 days before using.
7. Verify that the final pH level is approximately 5.5.

recipes.name: Fractionated Coconut & White Kaolin Clay Facial Balm
recipes.description: A simple, anhydrous cleansing balm formulated with rose petal powder and kaolin clay. Designed for easy melt and effective rinsing.
recipes.notes: Substitutions As always, be aware that making substitutions will change the final product. While these swaps won’t break the recipe, you will get a different final product than I did.
recipes.process:
1. Prepare a simmering water bath in a small saucepan.
2. Measure the heated phase ingredients into a heat-safe beaker and place it in the water bath.
3. Set up an ice bath in a separate bowl with cold water and ice cubes.
4. Heat the ingredients for 20–30 minutes until fully melted, then remove from heat and dry the container.
5. Place the beaker in the ice bath and stir steadily until the mixture reaches a "trace" consistency.
6. Pour the thickened balm into its final jar and allow it to set on the counter.
7. To use, massage a dollop of cleansing balm into dry skin and then wipe it off with a damp microfibre cloth.

recipes.name: Fractionated Coconut & Chamomile Facial Cream
recipes.description: A light, whipped cream cleanser formulated with sea buckthorn oil and calendula extract. Designed for a soft, airy texture and gentle use.

5. Combine the phases and allow the mixture to cool undisturbed until it solidifies.
6. Once solid, use an electric hand mixer to whip the cleanser until it is light, airy, and fluffy.
7. Apply a dollop to the skin and rinse away with a warm, damp cloth.

recipes.name: Fractionated Coconut & Cocamidopropyl Betaine Facial Cream
recipes.description: A jelly-textured facial cleanser utilizing polyacrylate crosspolymer-6 as a gelling agent. Provides a unique texture and gentle cleansing action.

recipes.process:
1. Measure the thickener and glycerin into a small beaker and stir until smooth.
2. Add the extract, oil, and preservative, then stir to combine.
3. Pour in the distilled water, cover the beaker, and allow the mixture to sit for several hours or overnight to fully hydrate.
4. Once the mixture is smooth and hydrated, whisk it vigorously until uniform.
5. Gently fold in the surfactant, noting that the texture will shift into a jelly-like consistency.
6. To use, lather a small amount with water in your hands before applying to the face.

recipes.name: C12-15 Alkyl Benzoate & Fractionated Coconut Facial Cream
recipes.description: A lightweight cleansing balm utilizing a blend of liquid emollients and surfactants for effective rinse-off. Designed for removing waterproof cosmetics.
recipes.notes: In order to keep this balm from feeling too heavy, the bulk of this Cream Silk Cleansing Balm is lightweight liquid emollients: C12-15 alkyl benzoate, sunflower seed oil, and fractionated coconut oil. If you’re looking to make substitutions, please prioritize keeping things fast-absorbing and inexpensive. I tried isopropyl myristate (IPM) instead of C12-15 alkyl benzoate and found that worke
recipes.process:
1. Set up a simmering water bath in a small saucepan with about 3cm of water.
2. Measure the ingredients into a heat-safe beaker and place it in the water bath until completely melted.
3. Prepare a cold ice bath in a separate bowl.
4. Remove the beaker from the heat once melted, dry the exterior, and place it on an insulated surface.
5. Transfer the beaker to the ice bath and stir steadily until the mixture reaches a thick "trace" consistency.
6. Pour the thickened balm into a wide-mouthed storage jar.
7. To use, massage into dry skin and remove with a warm, damp cloth.

recipes.name: Sweet Almond & Rose Facial Cream
recipes.description: An emulsified cream cleanser featuring honey and rose hydrosol. Can be used as a rinse-off or wipe-off cleanser.
recipes.notes: For scent, I just used a small amount of rose hydrosol from Plant’s Power, but you could easily customize the scent to your tastes. You could use water instead for an unscented product, or use a different hydrosol for a different scent. You could also incorporate an essential oil or fragrance oil—check out the links in the substitutions list below the formulation for details.
recipes.process:
1. Create a simmering water bath in a broad, flat-bottomed pan.
2. Measure the water phase ingredients into one heat-safe beaker and record the total weight.
3. Measure the oil phase ingredients into a second heat-safe beaker.
4. Heat both containers in the water bath until the oil phase is fully liquefied.
5. Combine the phases and mix thoroughly to form a uniform emulsion.
6. Allow the cream to cool before incorporating the cooling phase ingredients.
7. This product can be worked into a lather with water or applied directly to dry skin and wiped away with a damp cloth.

recipes.name: Finely Powdered Sodium Cocoyl Isethionate & Caprylyl/capryl Glucoside Facial Cream
recipes.description: A surfactant-infused cream cleanser formulated with aloe vera juice and calendula extract. Designed for gentle morning and evening use.
recipes.notes: We get our creamy goodness from three ingredients. Glyceryl Stearate SE is our emulsifier, while stearic acid and cetearyl alcohol both thicken the cleanser and add some lovely richness and emollience. If you wanted to make a thinner cleanser you could try swapping out a 2–3% from the stearic acid and/or cetearyl alcohol for a liquid oil.
recipes.process:
1. Prepare a simmering water bath in a broad, flat-bottomed pan.
2. Measure the oil phase ingredients into a heat-safe beaker and place it in the water bath until melted.
3. Blend the mixture for one to two minutes using a small high-powered mixer or immersion blender.
4. Transition to manual stirring and continue occasionally as the mixture cools to maintain a smooth texture.
5. Incorporate the cooling phase ingredients once the emulsion has reached room temperature.
6. Transfer the finished cleanser to a suitable storage container.

recipes.name: Lavender & Cocamidopropyl Betaine Facial Cream

recipes.name: Safflower & Fractionated Coconut Facial Oil

recipes.notes: I opted to leave this Soft Velvet Cleansing Oil unscented as I knew I’d be using it to remove eye makeup, but it’s pretty easy to make some room for an essential oil or fragrance oil if you want to include one. Simply drop 0.3–1% of one of the liquid oils, and voila, you’ve now got room for 0.3–1% of something that smells pretty!

5. Transfer the finished cleansing oil into a bottle for storage.

recipes.name: Fractionated Coconut & Cocoa Facial Balm

recipes.name: Sodium Cocoyl Isethionate & Cocamidopropyl Betaine Facial Solution
recipes.description: A solid foaming cleanser bar formulated with a skin-compatible pH. Features lavender essential oil and a creamy lather.
recipes.notes: Substitutions As always, be aware that making substitutions will change the final product. While these swaps won’t break the recipe, you will get a different final product than I did.
recipes.process:
1. Set up a simmering water bath with about 3cm of water in a small pan.
2. Measure the glycerin and thickener into a heat-safe beaker and whisk to combine.
3. Stir in the remaining surfactant phase ingredients and place the beaker in the water bath to heat through.
4. In a separate saucepan, melt the oil phase ingredients over low, direct heat.
5. Add the melted oil phase to the hot surfactant paste and stir well.
6. Remove from heat and continue stirring or mashing as the mixture cools to integrate the components.
7. Shape the resulting paste into bars and allow them to harden fully before use.

recipes.name: Rose & Caprylyl/capryl Glucoside Facial Solution
recipes.description: A liquid foaming cleanser utilizing Caprylyl/Capryl Glucoside as a primary surfactant and solubilizer. Designed for a pH-balanced, gentle cleanse.
recipes.notes: Another reason I’ve selected Caprylyl/Capryl Glucoside is that it is a good solubilizer for fragrance and essential oils—using it removes the need for a secondary solubilizer like Polysorbate 20. For this reason, I don’t recommend substituting it for a different glucoside surfactant, like coco glucoside or lauryl glucoside—they aren’t good solubilizers.
recipes.process:
1. Measure the surfactant and any essential or fragrance oils into a heat-safe beaker and stir to combine.
2. Add the remaining liquid ingredients one at a time, stirring steadily after each addition.
3. Incorporate the water and hydrosol last, stirring gently to avoid creating excessive foam.
4. Test the pH level and adjust it using a citric or lactic acid solution until it falls between 4.5 and 5.5.
5. Transfer the finished liquid into a foamer bottle.

recipes.name: Sweetgrass & Peg-6 Caprylic/capric Triglycerides Facial Solution

recipes.name: Sweetgrass & Iselux Ultra Mild Surfactant Blend Facial Solution

recipes.name: Dried Calendula Petals & Castor Facial Balm

If I want to add essential oils (or fragrance oils), when should I add them?
Add any essential oils to the cool down phase with the preservative, and then carry on with testing and adjusting the pH (if required). Adding a small percentage of essential oils to the formulation will not meaningfully impact the pH of your lotion. Essential oils don't have a pH value as they are not water soluble.
Could I add powdered goat milk?
You can definitely try it! The main concern with incorporating milk of any kind into a formulation is stability as milk is not known for being super shelf-stable, so you'll have to try it and then monitor the formulation for stability.
When starting to formulate with a new ingredient, a great way to get an idea for what can work is looking at sample formulations from suppliers and manufacturers. Lotion Crafter has a goat milk lotion formulation on their website and they note the "formula has passed a USP 51 Preservative Efficacy Test".
The formulation from Lotion Crafter uses 1% goat milk powder in their heated water phase, and that seems like a good place to start. Drop 1% of the distilled water to make room for the milk powder.
You'll notice the Lotion Crafter formulation includes a chelator (Disodium EDTA)—I'd probably incorporate one as well. They use Euxyl® PE 9010 (Phenoxyethanol [and] Ethylhexylglycerin), Potassium Sorbate, and Sodium Benzoate to preserve the formulation, and recommend a final pH of 4.5

recipes.name: Tkb Mousse Medium & Tkb Film Fix Cosmetic Cream

Dark rhassoul and French Red clay boost the bar’s slip and cleansing power, while contributing to the final colour. I’ll forgive you if you want to eat the bars, but I wouldn’t recommend it.

recipes.name: Sweet Almond & White Beeswax Body Lotion
recipes.description: Solid lotion bars featuring unrefined cocoa butter and white beeswax. Designed to melt upon contact with skin, providing a protective, long-lasting emollient layer.
recipes.process:
1. Melt the beeswax and carrier oils in a heat-safe container using 60-second microwave bursts.
2. Incorporate the cocoa butter and stir until fully melted, heating further if necessary.
3. Add the fragrance oils and stir thoroughly.
4. Place botanical decorations in the moulds and secure them with a thin layer of the liquid mixture.
5. Fill the moulds and flash-freeze for 30–60 minutes to prevent crystallization.

recipes.name: Avocado & White Beeswax Body Butter
recipes.description: Solid body butter in a convenient twist-up stick format. Formulated with avocado butter and beeswax for high stability and a non-greasy, protective skin finish.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the oils, butters, and waxes in a heat-safe container.
2. Melt using short microwave bursts until the beeswax is fully liquid.
3. Incorporate the fragrance and stir until uniform.
4. Pour the liquid mixture into twist-up tubes from the bottom.
5. Allow to set completely before securing the base caps.

recipes.name: Kaolin Clay & Avocado Body Mask
recipes.description: A detoxifying clay mask featuring pumpkin powder and Brazilian red clay. Formulated with BTMS-50 for a smooth, conditioning application and a non-stripping cleanse.
recipes.process:
1. Disinfect all utensils. Melt the oil phase and waxes in a water bath until liquid.
2. In a separate container, whisk the clays and botanical powders together.
3. Heat the distilled water to 70°C (160°F).
4. Merge the oil phase into the hot water and blend with an immersion blender for one minute.
5. Gradually incorporate the clay mixture while continuing to blend until a smooth, thick paste is achieved.
6. Adjust viscosity by heating slightly if the mixture becomes too cool to work.

recipes.name: Turmeric Shea & Coconut Body Butter
recipes.description: A vibrant whipped body butter featuring turmeric shea butter and ginger essential oil. Formulated for high emolliency and intensive skin nourishment with a soft, airy texture.
recipes.process:
1. Place the shea butter in a large mixing bowl and soften with an electric mixer.
2. Gradually incorporate the liquid oils while continuing to mix.
3. Add the botanical powders and essential oils.
4. Whip the mixture for several minutes until it reaches a light, fluffy consistency.
5. Transfer to storage jars and store in a cool location.

recipes.name: Oat & Oat Body Lotion
recipes.description: A high-viscosity emulsified lotion featuring colloidal oatmeal and oat extract. Designed for intensive hydration and a silky, cashmere-like skin finish.
recipes.process:
1. Heat the distilled water to 70°C (160°F) and blend in the colloidal oatmeal with an immersion blender.
2. Heat the oil phase and emulsifiers in a separate container until fully melted.
3. Merge the two phases and blend thoroughly for 90 seconds to ensure a stable emulsion.
4. Allow the lotion to cool to room temperature, then incorporate the fragrance and preservative.
5. Transfer to storage bottles and allow to set overnight.

recipes.name: Avocado & Seaweed Body Butter
recipes.description: A luxurious whipped body butter featuring avocado butter and reflective pearl powder. Designed for a luminous skin finish and intensive moisturizing benefits.
recipes.process:
1. Whip the avocado butter in a mixing bowl for 60 seconds to break up any clumps.
2. Incorporate the liquid extracts and fragrance, continuing to whip for 30 seconds.
3. Add the pearl powder and mica, blending well.
4. Fold in the starch and perform a final whip for 60 seconds until smooth and fluffy.
5. Transfer to wide-mouthed storage jars.

recipes.name: Kaolin Clay & Sea Clay Body Mask
recipes.description: A clarifying clay mask featuring seaweed extract and spirulina powder. Formulated with BTMS-50 and Polawax for a smooth, conditioning application and effective removal of excess sebum.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the clays and spirulina powder in a mixing bowl and whisk until uniform.
2. Melt the oil phase and waxes in a heat-safe container using a water bath or microwave.
3. Heat the distilled water to 70°C (160°F).
4. Gradually incorporate the clay mixture into the hot water while blending with an immersion blender.
5. Once the mixture is below 60°C (140°F), add the seaweed extract, essential oils, and preservative.
6. Perform a final blend until smooth and package in airtight glass jars.

recipes.name: Carrot & Cetearyl Alcohol Body Solution
recipes.description: A high-performance hair conditioner featuring carrot seed oil and extract. Designed to provide intensive conditioning and improved hair manageability with a skin-compatible pH.
recipes.process:
1. Heat the oil phase and conditioning emulsifiers in a water bath or microwave until the temperature reaches 82°C (180°F).
2. Heat the distilled water to 70–75°C and dissolve the panthenol.
3. Merge the two phases and blend thoroughly with an immersion blender for several minutes.
4. Once the emulsion has cooled to 60°C (140°F), incorporate the carrot extract, essential oils, and preservative.
5. Continue blending for 2–3 minutes and transfer to storage jars.

recipes.name: Jojoba & Orchid Body Lotion
recipes.description: A lightweight facial lotion featuring orchid extract and jojoba oil. Formulated for high stability and a smooth, non-greasy skin finish.
recipes.process:
1. Heat the distilled water to 70–82°C (160–180°F).
2. Heat the oil phase and emulsifiers in a separate container to the same temperature range.
3. Combine the phases and blend with an immersion blender for 60–90 seconds to ensure stable emulsification.
4. Allow the lotion to cool to room temperature, then incorporate the fragrance and preservative.
5. Transfer to storage bottles and allow to set undisturbed for 24 hours.

recipes.name: Lavender & Orchid Body Butter
recipes.description: A soothing whipped body butter featuring lavender essential oil and orchid extract. Formulated for a light, airy texture and intensive skin hydration.
recipes.process:
1. Soften the lavender butter in a large mixing bowl using a whisk attachment.
2. Incorporate the orchid extract and lavender essential oil, whisking until well blended.
3. Gradually add the starch and perform a final whip for 30 seconds until the mixture is fluffy and smooth.
4. Transfer to storage jars and tap firmly to settle the product.

recipes.name: Kaolin Clay & Avocado Body Mask
recipes.description: DIY Moringa Clay Mask DIY from Soap Queen.

recipes.name: Argan & Jojoba Body Oil
recipes.description: A versatile massage oil blend featuring argan, jojoba, and moringa oils. Formulated for high glide and customizable aromatherapeutic benefits.
recipes.process:
1. Combine all carrier oils in a small beaker or mixing container.
2. Incorporate the essential oil blend, adjusting the concentration based on preference.
3. Stir until the mixture is completely uniform.
4. Transfer to a storage bottle and store in a cool, dark location.

recipes.name: Moringa & Rosehip Body Lotion
recipes.description: A hydrating lotion featuring honeyquat and moringa seed oil. Formulated with allantoin for enhanced skin-soothing properties and a lightweight, fast-absorbing finish.
recipes.process:
1. Heat the oil phase and emulsifiers in a water bath or microwave until melted (approx. 70°C).
2. Dissolve the allantoin in hot distilled water (70°C) and whisk thoroughly.
3. Merge the two phases and blend with an immersion blender to form a stable emulsion.
4. Once the temperature drops to 55°C (130°F), incorporate the honeyquat and blend for 60 seconds.
5. Transfer the finished lotion to storage bottles.

recipes.name: Shea & Matcha Green Tea Body Butter
recipes.description: An antioxidant-rich body butter featuring matcha tea butter and shea butter. Formulated for high emolliency and a creamy, whipped consistency.
recipes.process:
1. Whip the shea butter in a mixing bowl for 1–2 minutes until smooth.
2. Incorporate the matcha tea butter and perform a secondary whip until the two are fully integrated.
3. Add the fragrance and preservative, whisking for an additional minute.
4. Fold in the starch and perform a final whip until the butter reaches a light, fluffy consistency.
5. Transfer to storage jars.

recipes.name: Moringa & Cetearyl Alcohol Body Oil
recipes.description: A nourishing hair conditioner featuring moringa seed oil and ginger essential oil. Designed for high performance and improved hair shine with a skin-compatible pH.
recipes.process:
1. Heat the distilled water to 70–82°C (160–180°F).
2. Heat the oil phase and conditioning emulsifiers to 82°C (180°F).
3. Merge the phases and blend with an immersion blender until stable.
4. Once the mixture drops to 60°C (140°F), incorporate the ginger essential oil.
5. Add the preservative once the temperature is below 50°C and perform a final blend for 60–90 seconds.

recipes.name: Avocado & Kokum Body Balm
recipes.description: A protective body balm featuring kokum butter and avocado oil. Formulated with Cera Bellina for a smooth, gel-like texture and scented with frankincense essential oil.
recipes.process:
1. Chop the kokum butter into small pieces for efficient melting.
2. Melt the butter, carrier oil, and waxes in a heat-safe container using short microwave bursts.
3. Stir until the mixture is uniform and the butter is fully dissolved.
4. Allow the mixture to cool below 47°C (117°F) before incorporating the frankincense essential oil.
5. Transfer to storage jars and allow to solidify completely.

recipes.name: Deodorized Cocoa & Polysorbate 80 Body Effervescent
recipes.description: Decorative bath bombs featuring a crystal-inspired design and high effervescence. Formulated with cocoa butter and Epsom salts for a skin-softening, mineral-rich bath experience.
recipes.process:
1. Melt the cocoa butter in a heat-safe container.
2. Incorporate the solubilizer and fragrance into the melted butter.
3. In a separate bowl, whisk the baking soda and citric acid until clump-free.
4. Gradually add the oil mixture to the powders and blend with gloved hands.
5. Create a salt slurry by mixing sea salt, glitter, and mica.
6. Layer the salt slurry and bath bomb mixture into moulds to create the crystal effect.
7. Allow the bombs to dry for 24 hours before unmoulding and decorating with mica paints.

recipes.name: Kaolin Clay & Castile  Soap Base Body Scrub
recipes.description: A detoxifying facial scrub featuring activated charcoal and liquid castile soap. Formulated with hazelnut and tamanu oils for deep cleansing without stripping natural lipids.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the liquid soap and carrier oils in a mixing bowl and stir until uniform.
2. Incorporate the essential oils and preservative.
3. In a separate container, whisk the clays and exfoliating beads together.
4. Gradually add the dry mixture to the liquid base in 3–4 batches, stirring well after each addition to ensure a smooth, clump-free paste.
5. Transfer to storage jars.

recipes.name: Foaming Bath & Sugar Body Scrub
recipes.description: A high-performance foaming sugar scrub featuring coffee butter and walnut shells. Designed for intensive physical exfoliation and a seasonal latte-inspired scent.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the foaming bath butter and coffee butter in a large bowl.
2. Whip with an electric mixer until the two are thoroughly integrated.
3. Incorporate the sugar and walnut shells, continuing to blend until the exfoliants are evenly distributed.
4. Add the fragrance oils and perform a final whip on low speed.
5. Transfer to storage jars.

recipes.name: Avocado & Meadowfoam Body Butter
recipes.description: DIY How to Make Whipped Body Butter on Soap Queen TV from Soap Queen.

recipes.name: Argan & Avocado Body Lotion
recipes.description: A foundational lotion bar base featuring white beeswax and liquid carrier oils. Formulated for high stability and a soothing lavender scent.
recipes.process:
1. Heat the base oils and waxes in a water bath until fully melted.
2. Remove from heat and incorporate the lavender essential oil.
3. Stir thoroughly until the mixture is uniform.
4. Pour into silicone moulds and allow to solidify completely.

recipes.name: Avocado & Cocoa  Chunks Body Butter
recipes.description: A luxurious whipped body mousse featuring avocado butter and unrefined cocoa butter. Designed for high emolliency and a soft, cashmere-like skin finish.
recipes.process:
1. Melt the cocoa butter and liquid oils in a heat-safe container.
2. Once melted, incorporate the fragrance and set aside to cool.
3. Whip the avocado butter in a separate bowl until smooth.
4. Gradually add the melted cocoa butter mixture to the avocado butter in four stages, whipping thoroughly after each addition.
5. Continue whipping for several minutes until the mousse reaches room temperature and is light and fluffy.

recipes.name: Olive & Shea Body Lotion
recipes.description: Nourishing lotion bars featuring unrefined honey fragrance and shea butter. Formulated for high emolliency and a smooth, protective finish that remains stable in moderate heat.
recipes.process:
1. Heat the base oils and waxes in a water bath until melted.
2. Remove from heat and stir in the shea butter until fully liquefied.
3. Incorporate the fragrance and stir until uniform.
4. Pour the liquid into silicone moulds and allow to solidify for several hours or overnight.

recipes.name: Avocado & Grapeseed Body Butter
recipes.description: A nutrient-rich whipped body butter featuring avocado butter and green tea extract. Formulated for high emolliency and a soft, airy texture with a skin-compatible pH.
recipes.process:
1. Soften the avocado butter in a large mixing bowl using a hand or stand mixer on medium speed for 2 minutes.
2. Gradually incorporate the liquid carrier oils, green tea extract, and fragrance.
3. Whip for one minute until the liquids are fully integrated.
4. Fold in the starch and perform a final whip for 2 minutes until the butter is light and fluffy.
5. Transfer to storage jars.

recipes.name: Sweet Almond & Emulsifying Body Lotion
recipes.description: A brightening facial lotion featuring argan oil and oat extract. Formulated for high stability and a lightweight, fast-absorbing skin finish.
recipes.process:
1. Heat the oil phase and emulsifiers in a water bath or microwave until the temperature reaches 70°C (160°F).
2. Heat the distilled water and humectants to the same temperature in a separate container.
3. Combine the phases and blend with an immersion blender to form a stable emulsion.
4. Once the mixture drops below 49°C (120°F), incorporate the active extracts and preservative.
5. Continue blending for 90 seconds and transfer to storage bottles.

recipes.name: Avocado & White Beeswax Body Lotion
recipes.description: Seasonal solid lotion bars featuring coffee butter and avocado oil. Designed to provide a protective, gingerbread-scented emollient layer that melts on skin contact.
recipes.process:
1. Melt the base oils, butters, and waxes in a heat-safe container using one-minute microwave bursts.
2. Stir in the fragrance oils until fully integrated.
3. Allow the mixture to cool below 60°C (140°F) before pouring into silicone moulds.
4. Allow the bars to solidify completely for several hours.
5. Optionally, decorate the set bars with a mica and alcohol slurry.

recipes.name: Avocado & Coffee Body Butter
recipes.description: A shimmering whipped body butter featuring avocado and coffee butters. Formulated with bronze-toned micas for a radiant skin finish and intensive hydration.
recipes.process:
1. Melt the cocoa butter phase and set aside to cool below 49°C (120°F).
2. Whip the avocado and coffee butters in a separate bowl until smooth.
3. Gradually incorporate the melted cocoa butter into the whipped base, blending thoroughly.
4. Add the fragrance, starch, and mica shimmer.
5. Perform a final whip for several minutes until fluffy and transfer to storage jars.

recipes.name: Aloe Vera & Bottles White Disk Cap Body Solution
recipes.description: A hydrating rose and aloe-based emulsion formulated with green tea seed oil. Designed for high conditioning performance and intensive skin nourishment.
recipes.process:
1. Heat the oil phase and emulsifiers in a water bath until fully melted.
2. Heat the aloe vera liquid to 65°C (150°F) and dissolve the panthenol.
3. Combine the phases and blend with an immersion blender to form a stable emulsion.
4. Once the mixture is below 49°C (120°F), incorporate the extracts and preservative.
5. Continue blending and transfer to storage bottles when the temperature is below 43°C (110°F).

recipes.name: Potassium Cocoate Body Oil
recipes.description: A professional-grade liquid shampoo featuring argan oil and Potassium Cocoate. Designed for effective hair cleansing and improved shine with a skin-compatible pH.
recipes.process:
1. Disinfect all utensils. Heat the distilled water to 65°C (150°F).
2. Heat the surfactant phase and argan oil in a separate container to 65°C (150°F).
3. Merge the phases and blend with an immersion blender for 20 seconds.
4. Once the temperature drops below 60°C (140°F), incorporate the extracts, fragrance, and preservative.
5. Transfer to storage bottles and allow to set overnight.

recipes.name: Tall Plastic Bail Jar & Fractionated Coconut Body Butter
recipes.description: An intensive anhydrous balm for dry heels featuring shea butter and Cera Bellina. Designed for long-lasting protection and high skin-lipid replenishment.
recipes.process:
1. Combine the liquid carrier oils in a large container.
2. Melt the butter phase and waxes in a separate heat-safe beaker until liquid.
3. Incorporate the melted wax mixture into the oil mixture and stir until uniform.
4. Transfer to a storage jar and allow it to solidify for 4 hours.

recipes.name: Bottle With Pump Top & Aloe Vera Body Lotion
recipes.description: DIY Argan & Shea Lotion from Soap Queen.

recipes.name: Coffee & Rice Bran Body Butter
recipes.description: An energizing whipped body butter featuring coffee butter and tamanu oil. Formulated for high emolliency and a soft, airy texture with a natural coffee aroma.
recipes.process:
1. Whip the coffee butter on low speed for one minute to soften the texture.
2. Gradually incorporate the liquid carrier oils and fragrances while continuing to whip.
3. Increase the mixer speed and whip until the butter reaches a light, fluffy consistency.
4. Transfer to storage jars and tap to settle the product.

recipes.name: Coconut & White Beeswax Body Solution
recipes.description: DIY How to Make Perfume Video from Soap Queen.

recipes.name: Avocado & Meadowfoam Body Balm
recipes.description: A protective winter body balm formulated with candelilla wax and meadowfoam oil. Designed for high stability and intensive hydration in cold environmental conditions.
recipes.process:
1. Melt the waxes and carrier oils in a heat-safe container until fully liquid.
2. Stir in the avocado butter until melted and uniform.
3. Incorporate the fragrance and botanical extracts.
